<translate>
<!--T:1-->
'''Weapon Attributes''' is a datapack system that tells the DragonMineZ combat engine how a specific item behaves in combat: attack range, animation, hitbox shape, damage multipliers, conditional attack variants (dual-wielding, sneaking, mounted and so on) and critical stats. Third-party weapon mods hook into this system to get proper DragonMineZ combat behavior.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:2-->
Loader: <code>WeaponRegistry.loadAttributes(resourceManager)</code>, in <code>src/main/java/com/dragonminez/common/combat/logic/weapon/WeaponRegistry.java</code>. It reloads with the vanilla datapack reload (<code>/reload</code> or a restart), '''not''' with <code>/dmzreload</code>.
</translate>

<translate>
== File location and item mapping == <!--T:3-->
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
data/<namespace>/weapon_attributes/<item_path>.json
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:4-->
The namespace and path become the target item id: <code>data/dragonminez/weapon_attributes/axe.json</code> applies to <code>dragonminez:axe</code>. A third-party mod defines its own weapons under its own namespace, for example <code>data/mymod/weapon_attributes/great_axe.json</code> for <code>mymod:great_axe</code>.
</translate>

{{Note|title=<translate><!--T:5--> Better Combat datapacks</translate>|text=<translate><!--T:6--> Any <code>bettercombat:</code> namespace found in these JSON files is rewritten to <code>dragonminez:</code> at load time, so weapon attribute datapacks written for the Better Combat mod mostly work as they are.</translate>}}

<translate>
== Top-level schema == <!--T:7-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:8-->
A file holds an <code>attributes</code> object:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
{
  "attributes": { ... }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:9-->
Or, to inherit another item's attributes and only override specific fields, it names a <code>parent</code>:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
{
  "parent": "dragonminez:sword",
  "attributes": {
    "crit_chance": 0.10,
    "crit_damage": 0.15
  }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:10-->
<code>parent</code> chains can go several levels deep (a parent can have its own parent). Cycles are detected: a weapon whose parent chain loops back on itself fails to resolve and is skipped (logged as an error), so double-check your <code>parent</code> references.
</translate>

<translate>
== Attributes fields == <!--T:11-->
</translate>
{{Config|Combat Config|fallbackCompatibility}}

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:12--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:13--> Type</translate> !! <translate><!--T:14--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>attack_range</code> || <translate><!--T:15--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:16--> Reach in blocks (the Minecraft default <code>3.0</code> if left out).</translate>
|-
| <code>pose</code> || <translate><!--T:17--> String</translate> || <translate><!--T:18--> GeckoLib animation pose for the main-hand weapon.</translate>
|-
| <code>off_hand_pose</code> || <translate><!--T:19--> String</translate> || <translate><!--T:20--> GeckoLib animation pose for the off-hand weapon.</translate>
|-
| <code>two_handed</code> || <translate><!--T:21--> Boolean</translate> || <translate><!--T:22--> If <code>true</code>, the off hand can't be used while the weapon is wielded.</translate>
|-
| <code>category</code> || <translate><!--T:23--> String</translate> || <translate><!--T:24--> Free-form category tag. It is used for two things: matching <code>DUAL_WIELDING_SAME_CATEGORY</code> conditions between the main hand and the off hand, '''and''' as the target category for the <code>fallbackCompatibility</code> regex system in [[Special:MyLanguage/Combat Config|Combat Config]].</translate>
|-
| <code>crit_chance</code> || <translate><!--T:25--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:26--> Innate critical chance (<code>0.0</code>–<code>1.0</code>), applied as an attribute modifier.</translate>
|-
| <code>crit_damage</code> || <translate><!--T:27--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:28--> Innate critical damage multiplier, applied as an attribute modifier.</translate>
|-
| <code>attacks</code> || <translate><!--T:29--> Array</translate> || <translate><!--T:30--> '''Required.''' One or more attack variants (see below).</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Attack entries == <!--T:31-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:32-->
Each entry of <code>attacks</code> describes one swing variant. DragonMineZ checks the <code>conditions</code> from top to bottom and uses the first attack whose conditions all pass.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:33--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:34--> Type</translate> !! <translate><!--T:35--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>conditions</code> || <translate><!--T:36--> List of condition strings</translate> || <translate><!--T:37--> All of them must be true for this variant to fire. Leave it out for an unconditional attack.</translate>
|-
| <code>hitbox</code> || <translate><!--T:38--> String</translate> || <translate><!--T:39--> <code>FORWARD_BOX</code> (a box extending forward, closest to vanilla), <code>VERTICAL_PLANE</code> (a vertical sweeping slash) or <code>HORIZONTAL_PLANE</code> (a wide horizontal sweep).</translate>
|-
| <code>damage_multiplier</code> || <translate><!--T:40--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:41--> Multiplier on the weapon's base damage (default <code>1.0</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>angle</code> || <translate><!--T:42--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:43--> Swing arc in degrees.</translate>
|-
| <code>upswing</code> || <translate><!--T:44--> Number</translate> || <translate><!--T:45--> Cooldown multiplier: <code>cooldownTicks = (1 / (4 - attackSpeed)) * 20 * upswing</code>. Lower means a faster follow-up. It also sets the swing's '''windup''' (the delay before the hit lands): animation ticks × <code>upswing</code> × 0.95, clamped to 3–7 ticks.</translate>
|-
| <code>animation</code> || <translate><!--T:46--> String</translate> || <translate><!--T:47--> GeckoLib animation name. It is checked against <code>animations/*.json</code>; if there is no exact match, DragonMineZ picks the closest name (Levenshtein distance) after stripping known prefixes (<code>dragonminez:</code>, <code>bettercombat:</code>, <code>combat.</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>swing_sound</code> / <code>impact_sound</code> || <code>{ "id", "volume"*, "pitch"*, "randomness"* }</code> || <translate><!--T:48--> Sound played on swing or impact. <code>volume</code> and <code>pitch</code> default to <code>1.0</code>, <code>randomness</code> to <code>0.1</code>.</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== Attack conditions === <!--T:49-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:50-->
This is the complete list of conditions:
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:51--> Condition</translate> !! <translate><!--T:52--> Meaning</translate>
|-
| <code>NOT_DUAL_WIELDING</code> || <translate><!--T:53--> The off hand is empty (air).</translate>
|-
| <code>DUAL_WIELDING_ANY</code> || <translate><!--T:54--> Both hands hold something.</translate>
|-
| <code>DUAL_WIELDING_SAME</code> || <translate><!--T:55--> Both hands hold the exact same item id.</translate>
|-
| <code>DUAL_WIELDING_SAME_CATEGORY</code> || <translate><!--T:56--> Both hands hold items that share the same <code>category</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>NO_OFFHAND_ITEM</code> || <translate><!--T:57--> The off hand is empty.</translate>
|-
| <code>OFF_HAND_SHIELD</code> || <translate><!--T:58--> The off hand holds a shield.</translate>
|-
| <code>MAIN_HAND_ONLY</code> || <translate><!--T:59--> The attack only applies to the main-hand weapon.</translate>
|-
| <code>OFF_HAND_ONLY</code> || <translate><!--T:60--> The attack only applies to the off-hand weapon.</translate>
|-
| <code>MOUNTED</code> || <translate><!--T:61--> The player is riding an entity.</translate>
|-
| <code>NOT_MOUNTED</code> || <translate><!--T:62--> The player is not riding.</translate>
|-
| <code>SNEAKING</code> || <translate><!--T:63--> The player is crouching.</translate>
|-
| <code>NOT_SNEAKING</code> || <translate><!--T:64--> The player is standing.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Full example == <!--T:65-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:66-->
A dagger with several attacks and a dual-wield variant:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
{
  "attributes": {
    "attack_range": 2,
    "two_handed": false,
    "category": "dagger",
    "attacks": [
      {
        "hitbox": "HORIZONTAL_PLANE",
        "damage_multiplier": 0.8,
        "angle": 150,
        "upswing": 0.5,
        "animation": "combat.one_handed_slash_horizontal_right_1",
        "swing_sound": { "id": "dragonminez:dagger_slash" }
      },
      {
        "hitbox": "HORIZONTAL_PLANE",
        "damage_multiplier": 0.8,
        "angle": 150,
        "upswing": 0.5,
        "animation": "combat.one_handed_slash_horizontal_right_2",
        "swing_sound": { "id": "dragonminez:dagger_slash" }
      },
      {
        "conditions": ["DUAL_WIELDING_SAME_CATEGORY", "MAIN_HAND_ONLY"],
        "hitbox": "FORWARD_BOX",
        "damage_multiplier": 1.4,
        "angle": 150,
        "upswing": 0.5,
        "animation": "combat.dual_handed_stab",
        "swing_sound": { "id": "dragonminez:dagger_slash" }
      }
    ]
  }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:67-->
An inheritance example (<code>brave_sword.json</code>, overriding only the critical stats):
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
{
  "parent": "dragonminez:sword",
  "attributes": {
    "crit_chance": 0.10,
    "crit_damage": 0.15
  }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
== Shipped attribute files == <!--T:68-->
</translate>
{{See also|Special Weapons}}
<translate>
<!--T:69-->
DragonMineZ ships these entries under <code>data/dragonminez/weapon_attributes/</code>, so you can use them as a <code>parent</code> or as a <code>weaponCombo</code> or fallback target:
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:70-->
* '''Base movesets:''' <code>anchor</code>, <code>axe</code>, <code>battlestaff</code>, <code>claw</code>, <code>claymore</code>, <code>cutlass</code>, <code>dagger</code>, <code>double_axe</code>, <code>fist</code>, <code>giant</code>, <code>glaive</code>, <code>halberd</code>, <code>hammer</code>, <code>katana</code>, <code>lance</code>, <code>mace</code>, <code>pickaxe</code>, <code>rapier</code>, <code>scythe</code>, <code>sickle</code>, <code>soul_knife</code>, <code>spear</code>, <code>staff</code>, <code>sword</code>, <code>trident</code>, <code>twin_blade</code>, <code>wand</code>.
* '''Signature weapons:''' <code>brave_sword</code> ([[Special:MyLanguage/Brave Sword|Brave Sword]], parent <code>sword</code>), <code>yajirobe_katana</code> ([[Special:MyLanguage/Yajirobe's Katana|Yajirobe's Katana]], parent <code>katana</code>), <code>z_sword</code> ([[Special:MyLanguage/Z Sword|Z Sword]], parent <code>claymore</code>) and <code>power_pole</code> ([[Special:MyLanguage/Power Pole|Power Pole]], parent <code>staff</code>, with its own three-hit combo).
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:71-->
DragonMineZ items without an entry of their own (for example the [[Special:MyLanguage/Dimension Sword|Dimension Sword]] and the Tamagami weapons: [[Special:MyLanguage/Tamagami Sword|Tamagami Sword]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Tamagami Trident|Tamagami Trident]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Tamagami Hammer|Tamagami Hammer]]) get their moveset from the <code>fallbackCompatibility</code> regexes in [[Special:MyLanguage/Combat Config|Combat Config]], just like third-party weapons.
</translate>

<translate>
== For third-party weapon mods == <!--T:72-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:73-->
If your mod adds weapons and you don't ship a Weapon Attributes entry for them, DragonMineZ falls back to matching the item id of every item with an attack-damage modifier against the <code>fallbackCompatibility</code> list in [[Special:MyLanguage/Combat Config|Combat Config]] (for example, an item id containing <code>axe</code> is treated like <code>dragonminez:axe</code>). This gives a reasonable default, but a real datapack entry that matches your weapon's actual moveset and animations is always more accurate, and it always takes priority over the fallback guess.
</translate>

<translate>
== Reload and validate == <!--T:74-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:75-->
# Add or edit files under <code>data/<namespace>/weapon_attributes/</code>.
# Validate the JSON syntax (see [[Special:MyLanguage/How to JSON|How to JSON]]).
# Run the vanilla <code>/reload</code>, or restart. This is a plain datapack reload listener, not part of <code>/dmzreload</code> (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Reloading and Updating Changes|Reloading and Updating Changes]]).
# Test the weapon in game: range, animation, hitbox shape and any conditional variants (dual-wielding, sneaking, mounted).
</translate>

{{Navbox Modding}}
